Why · How · What Why AI needs a brief, how five moves and five principles give it one, and what the Explorable shows. Why You brief an AI, and it forgets, guesses and still sounds sure. Every new chat starts from zero, and when it is unsure it answers anyway instead of asking. ( ) Five traits, PRICE, explain why it costs you, side by side for a freelancer and for AI. How Five moves brief one agent: BRIEF. Break it down, put requirements first, interview yourself with AI, evaluate each step and start fresh for each piece. ( ) Each move counters one or more of the five traits. What Five principles run the work across stages: BRACE. Start backwards from the goal, resolve dependencies early, give autonomy through intent, agree contracts at the seams and engineer trust. ( ) See them on DRIVE: Define, Reason, Implement, Verify, Evolve.

About The forgetting and the guessing are built in The context window is the model's working memory, and memory across chats exists only where an application stores notes and puts them back, because the memory tool runs client-side 1 2 . Most benchmarks score a guess above an abstention, so training rewards guessing instead of asking 3 (Episode evidence: Pay the price). Sources (3) Anthropic, Context windows ( opens in a new tab ) platform.claude.com Anthropic, Memory tool ( opens in a new tab ) platform.claude.com Kalai et al., Why Language Models Hallucinate ( opens in a new tab ) arxiv.org Each move has evidence behind it Solving simpler subproblems in sequence scored 99% or better on a compositional benchmark against 16% for chain-of-thought prompting with an older model 1 . Results varied more than twice as much for a requirement left unstated as for one stated 2 . Feedback on each reasoning step beats feedback on the final result alone 3 . Top models scored on average 39% lower in multi-turn conversation than with the full instruction at once 4 (Episode evidence: Manage the price). "Interview yourself with AI" is backed by two further studies there. Sources (4) Zhou et al., Least-to-Most Prompting Enables Complex Reasoning in Large Language Models ( opens in a new tab ) arxiv.org Yang, Shi, Ma, Liu, Kästner, Wu, What Prompts Don't Say: Understanding and Managing Underspecification in LLM Prompts (v3) ( opens in a new tab ) arxiv.org Lightman et al., Let's Verify Step by Step ( opens in a new tab ) arxiv.org Laban et al., LLMs Get Lost in Multi-Turn Conversation ( opens in a new tab ) arxiv.org BRACE: five principles, each with its own source Anthropic tells builders to define success criteria up front 1 . Planning backwards from the goal is established practice in planning, but no study tests it on agent work (research PLAN-0003). Subagents without detailed tasks "duplicate work, leave gaps, or fail to find necessary information", and multi-agent systems are a poor fit where many dependencies run between agents 2 (research SWE-0007, SWE-0008). Army doctrine tells commanders to state the results to be attained, not how, and says trust "must be earned" 3 (research AIE-0027). Reliance should match demonstrated reliability 4 , and agents need checkpoints, guardrails and ground truth from the environment 5 (research AIE-0028).
